causes.label: wind_output
causes.quote: During the 30-minute period of high prices, combined NSW and Queensland wind generation was low, averaging 551 MW. During the same time in the preceding week, the average wind generation was 926 MW.

causes.label: scheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: Four baseload units in NSW and four in Queensland were unavailable at the time of the high prices totalling 4,185 MW (Table 2). Three of these were planned, the other five were unplanned as follows:

causes.label: unscheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: Four baseload units in NSW and four in Queensland were unavailable at the time of the high prices totalling 4,185 MW (Table 2). Three of these were planned, the other five were unplanned as follows:

causes.label: network_outage
causes.quote: Planned outages of the Collector to Marulan and Canberra to Lower Tumut lines curtailed between 307 MW and 378 MW of low-priced capacity in southern NSW.

causes.label: rebids
causes.quote: Rebidding for technical reasons contributed to the high prices (Appendix A).

intervals.quote: On 9 April, at 5.30 pm the 30-minute price reached $6,191 per MWh in NSW and $5,434 per MWh in Queensland.

causes.label: wind_output
causes.quote: During the high-priced periods, average wind generation was around 200 MW. During the same hour in the week prior, the average wind generation was around 900 MW.

causes.label: scheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: Origin Energy's Eraring unit 3 and EnergyAustralia's Mount Piper unit 1 were on planned outages.

causes.label: unscheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: AGL's Bayswater unit 3 was on an unplanned outage due to unexpected plant limits that started on 2 May.

causes.label: ramp_rates
causes.quote: Snowy Hydro's Colongra Power Station could not start up quickly enough, which meant up to 125 MW of low-priced capacity could not make it to market, impacting two high-priced dispatch intervals.

causes.label: rebids
causes.quote: Rebidding for technical reasons contributed to high prices (Appendix B).

causes.label: demand
causes.quote: Evening peak demand when the prices were high increased from an average of 24,664 MW in April and 26,279 MW in May to 29,836 MW in June. June experienced the highest average demand since 2021.

causes.label: wind_output
causes.quote: During the high prices, wind generation across the NEM was around 1,400 MW. During the week preceding, at the same time of day, average wind generation was around 4,730 MW.

causes.label: scheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: A combination of planned and unplanned baseload outages across seven units meant that there was around 3,100 MW of generally low-priced capacity unavailable. These outages had occurred at least three days before the high prices (Table 3).

causes.label: unscheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: A combination of planned and unplanned baseload outages across seven units meant that there was around 3,100 MW of generally low-priced capacity unavailable. These outages had occurred at least three days before the high prices (Table 3).

causes.label: ramp_rates
causes.quote: Around 100 MW of low-priced capacity, most of which was at EnergyAustralia's Mount Piper Power Station, could not ramp up fast enough to prevent high prices.

causes.label: fcas_co_optimisation
causes.quote: Across all regions, up to 71 MW was unable to be dispatched due to technical parameters of generating units that provide energy and FCAS at the same time.

causes.label: battery_state_of_charge
causes.quote: Starting at 5.14 pm, across two batteries, Neoen shifted 84 MW and 245 MW of low-priced capacity to high prices for 5.35 pm and 5.50 pm, respectively. The rebids were primarily for charge management.

causes.quote: Evening peak demand when the prices were high increased from an average of 24,664 MW in April and 26,279 MW in May to 29,836 MW in June. June experienced the highest average demand since 2021.

causes.label: wind_output
causes.quote: As a result of calm conditions, wind output across the NEM was low. During the high-priced periods, total wind generation was around 900 MW. During the week prior, at the same time of day, wind generation was 4,574 MW.

causes.label: scheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: A combination of planned and unplanned baseload outages meant that there was around 3,100 MW of generally low-priced capacity unavailable (Table 3). Most of this capacity had been unavailable for at least three days in the lead up to the high prices.

causes.label: unscheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: A combination of planned and unplanned baseload outages meant that there was around 3,100 MW of generally low-priced capacity unavailable (Table 3). Most of this capacity had been unavailable for at least three days in the lead up to the high prices.

causes.label: ramp_rates
causes.quote: Between 41 MW and 95 MW of capacity at Vales Point was unable to be dispatched as it was being limited by its ramp-up rate.

causes.label: fcas_co_optimisation
causes.quote: Across all regions, up to 77 MW of capacity was unable to be dispatched due to technical parameters of generating units that provide energy and FCAS at the same time.

causes.label: battery_state_of_charge
causes.quote: Shell Energy's Rangebank Battery was being dispatched at around 200 MW from 5 pm until it had no availability left at 6.45 pm. Similarly, their Koorangie Battery was being dispatched for 185 MW until it removed all its available capacity from 7 pm.

causes.label: rebids
causes.quote: Rebidding for both technical and commercial reasons contributed to the high prices during intervals where amounts of high-price capacity required was low.

causes.label: demand
causes.quote: Evening peak demand when the prices were high increased from an average of 24,664 MW in April and 26,279 MW in May to 29,836 MW in June. June experienced the highest average demand since 2021.

causes.label: wind_output
causes.quote: Due to calm conditions, wind output across the NEM was low at the time of the high-priced periods. The total wind generation was around 260 MW, compared to the average wind generation of 4,620 MW during the same time of day in the preceding week.

causes.label: unscheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: At the time of the high prices, Victoria and NSW each had two unplanned coal unit outages. This meant 2,325 MW of baseload capacity, most of which is typically offered at low prices, was unavailable during the high prices (Table 3).

causes.label: battery_state_of_charge
causes.quote: Neoen in South Australia rebid its Blyth Battery capacity from both low to high and high to low prices due to a change in its state of charge, and effectively shifted a net capacity of 100 MW from low to high prices impacting the high price at 5.30pm.

causes.label: fcas_co_optimisation
causes.quote: In Tasmania, during one hour of high prices, prices were set by co-optimisation between energy and FCAS markets.

causes.label: rebids
causes.quote: Rebidding for both technical and commercial reasons contributed to the high prices.

intervals.quote: On 26 June, 30-minute energy prices exceeded $5,000 per MWh from 5.30 pm to 9 pm in NSW, Victoria and South Australia, and from 6 pm to 6.30 pm in Tasmania.
